newsitem.title: CANADA: Alliance formulating response to NOVA proposal.
newsitem.headline: Alliance formulating response to NOVA proposal.

text.p: Alliance Pipeline is working up a response to a NOVA Corp proposal that would see NOVA's pipeline system act as the Alberta portion of the Canada-Chicago pipeline project, an Alliance official said on Tuesday.

"It's fair to say that NOVA has approached us, that NOVA has made a proposal to us and we're in the process of formulating a response," Alliance vice-president Jack Crawford said in a telephone interview.
He said it was not yet known what the response would be or when a decision would be made.

NOVA president Jeff Lipton revealed on Tuesday that his company expected to start talks with the producer-backed Alliance pipeline, so far its most credible potential competitor in Alberta's gas pipeline business.

Crawford said NOVA Gas Transmission began recently talking to Alliance's owners, which include such firms as Chauvco Resources Ltd, IPL Energy and Alberta Energy Co, after the maverick pipeline announced it had 98 percent of its capacity committed under long-term contracts.
The owners deferred discussions to Alliance's operating company, he said.
The high producer support for the C$3.6-billion Alliance project and a continuing regulatory application process in Canada and the United States likely convinced NOVA to make the overture, he said.
"All of these things add credibility and credence to our project. I guess some folks sat up and took notice," Crawford said.
He said Alliance's objective from the start of its development was to get shippers' gas to the key U.S. Midwest market for the lowest cost, and that continued to be the case.
Producers have often said the traditional pipeline companies had contributed to low prices fetched for Canadian gas by not providing enough export capacity.
NOVA has contended that its system represented the lowest cost solution for Alberta gas producers and that the duplication of pipeline systems would only increase transport costs for the industry.
Under current plans, Alliance would start shipping liquids-rich gas the 3,000 kms to Chicago from northern Canada starting in 1999.
Crawford said NOVA likely had the capacity to ship some of the gas liquids envisioned to be moved on Alliance, although not all.
